Internal helper: where a table's N goes (rulings R51 and R59)

Source: R/tables.R
dot-jst_table_n_parts.Rd

n.position = title adds "(N = 103)" after the title, the call's own included – apa's value, and so report's, since ruling R59 (Session 409; built Session 410); note opens the general note on N; none writes no N. Under title a table whose ns vary – variables or models whose Ns differ, pairwise ns – gets the note's sentence instead, as note writes it (R59: "If the n varies within a table, I think we'll need to at that time only, place the n's in the note instead."). A table with no one N to write (variables from different pools of cases) gets nothing under any setting. The text is marked up for the writers (N italic).

Usage

.jst_table_n_parts(setting, n_text, varies = FALSE)

Arguments

setting

The n.position value.

n_text

NULL, or the sentence's body: "N = 103", or the form for ns that vary ("N differs by model: ...").

varies

TRUE when the table's ns vary, so the sentence goes in the note under title as under note.

Value

A list: note (character(0) or the sentence) and title ("" or the parenthesis to append).
